Visual "Table 1": summary table with inline distribution graphics

Source: R/table1viz.R
table1viz.Rd

Summarizes numeric and categorical variables for a cohort (optionally by group) like table_overall() / table_overall_and_group(), but adds compact inline graphics inspired by Furmaga et al. 2026:

Usage

table1viz(
  d,
  name_groupvar = NULL,
  overall = TRUE,
  group_header = "**Group**",
  stats_col_label = "Overall",
  missing = c("ifany", "no", "always"),
  missing_group = c("exclude", "show"),
  show_denominator = c("ifmissing", "always", "no"),
  statistic = list(gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", "{min}; {max}"),
    gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c("{n} ({p}%)")),
  digits = NULL,
  binary_01_only_show1 = TRUE,
  continuous_plot = c("violin_box", "boxplot", "density"),
  show_outliers = TRUE,
  show_axis = TRUE,
  axis_breaks = NULL,
  bar_axis = FALSE,
  bar_axis_breaks = c(0, 50, 100),
  colors = NULL,
  overall_color = "#7F7F7F",
  plot_width = 140,
  plot_height = 30,
  bar_width = 60,
  plot_layout = c("combined", "columns"),
  distribution_label = "**Distribution**",
  header_align = c("left", "center"),
  overall_divider = TRUE,
  variable_divider = TRUE,
  row_lines = FALSE,
  output = c("auto", "gt", "flextable")
)

Arguments

d

data.frame. Dataset containing variables to summarize.

name_groupvar

character(1) or NULL. Optional name of a grouping variable in d. If NULL (default) the entire cohort is summarized. Rows with a missing group are dropped (and counted in a table note) unless missing_group = "show".

overall

logical(1). If grouping, also show an Overall column? Default TRUE.

group_header

character(1). Spanning header over the group columns.

stats_col_label

character(1). Header label for the overall column.

missing

character(1). When to show an "N missing" row for each variable: "ifany" (default), "no", or "always". The row shows n / N (%) missing (n (%) if show_denominator = "no"), where N and % are out of all observations in the column, with a hatched bar on the same 0-100% scale as the category bars.

missing_group

character(1). Rows with a missing name_groupvar: "exclude" (default) drops them and reports how many in a table note; "show" keeps them as an extra "Missing" group column (colored brown, #8C564B, unless colors is named and includes "Missing").

show_denominator

character(1). When to show category counts as n / N (%) instead of n (%), where N is the number of non-missing values in the column (the percentage's denominator): "ifmissing" (default) for categorical variables with missing values, so the denominator is visible when it differs from the column N; "always" for all categorical variables; or "no". Only applies to variables whose statistic is the default "{n} ({p}%)". Unless "no", "N missing" rows also show n / N (%), with N the total number of observations in the column.

statistic, digits

Passed to gtsummary::tbl_summary(). By default continuous variables show mean (SD) and min; max; the graphic already shows the median and quartiles. For skewed variables, consider adding a "Median (Q1, Q3)" row with e.g. statistic = list(gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", "{median} ({p25}, {p75})", "{min}; {max}"), gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"). digits = NULL (default) lets gtsummary choose the decimals for each variable from its spread, so variables on a small scale (e.g. 0.03) are not rounded to 0.0; pass e.g. list(gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1) to fix them.

binary_01_only_show1

logical(1). If TRUE, binary variables only show one row (e.g. the "1"/"Yes" level). Default TRUE.

continuous_plot

character(1). Graphic for continuous variables: "violin_box" (violin with inner boxplot and outlier dots; default), "boxplot" (boxplot with outlier dots), or "density" (density sparkline with a tick at the median).

show_outliers

logical(1). Draw outliers (values beyond 1.5 x IQR from the box) as dots? Default TRUE. Whiskers still stop at the most extreme values within 1.5 x IQR when FALSE. Has no effect for continuous_plot = "density".

show_axis

logical(1). Add a small x-axis with a few tick labels under each continuous-variable graphic to show its range? Default TRUE. The axis is shared by all columns/groups of a variable.

axis_breaks

Optional named list giving tick values for specific continuous variables when show_axis = TRUE, e.g. list(age = c(20, 40, 60, 80)). Names are variable names in d; variables not listed get automatic ticks. Ticks outside the data range widen that variable's (shared) scale so they are shown. If a vector has names, they are used as the tick labels, e.g. c("0" = 0, "1 yr" = 365).

bar_axis

logical(1). Add a small 0-100% x-axis under the percentage bars? Default FALSE. The axis is drawn once per variable, under its last bar (the "N missing" row if shown, otherwise the last level).

bar_axis_breaks

numeric. Tick positions, in percent (0-100), for the bar axis when bar_axis = TRUE. Default c(0, 50, 100), labelled "0%", "50%", "100%". If the vector has names, they are used as the tick labels, e.g. c("0" = 0, "1/4" = 25, "1/2" = 50).

colors

Optional character vector of colors for the group columns (unnamed in group order, or named by group level). Defaults to the Okabe-Ito palette.

overall_color

character(1). Color used for the overall column.

plot_width, plot_height

numeric(1). Size of continuous-variable graphics in pixels.

bar_width

numeric(1). Width of percentage bars in pixels (plot_layout = "columns" only).

plot_layout

character(1). Where graphics go when grouping: "combined" (default) adds one "Distribution" column on the right in which the groups (and Overall) are drawn together on a shared axis, one lane per group, so they can be compared directly. Continuous variables get stacked violins/boxplots/densities spanning the variable's label and statistic rows; each categorical level gets a set of side-by-side bars. "columns" instead draws a separate graphic in each group's column. Ignored when name_groupvar is NULL.

distribution_label

character(1). Header of the combined distribution column.

header_align

character(1). Alignment of the column headers for the Overall, group and Distribution columns: "left" (default) or "center".

overall_divider

logical(1). Draw a vertical line to the right of the Overall column to set it apart from the group columns? Default TRUE. Only used when grouping with overall = TRUE.

variable_divider

logical(1). Draw a thicker horizontal line above each variable (except the first) so it is clearer where a new variable starts? Default TRUE.

row_lines

logical(1). Draw the thin horizontal lines between the rows within a variable (e.g. between its statistic rows or levels)? Default FALSE, so only the lines between variables are drawn. Applies to gt output; the Word (flextable) table has no lines within a variable.

output

character(1). Table type to return: "auto" (default) returns a flextable when knitting to Word (.docx, e.g. Quarto format: docx) and a gt table otherwise; "gt" or "flextable" force one. Requires the flextable and xml2 packages for "flextable".

Value

A gt::gt_tbl (output = "gt") or a flextable with class "table1viz_flextable" (output = "flextable").

The gt table draws graphics as inline SVG, so it renders in HTML output (Quarto/R Markdown HTML, RStudio viewer, gt::gtsave(".html")).

The flextable is for Word. When knitted to .docx it becomes a native, editable Word table: text, fonts, borders and widths can be edited in Word, and the graphics are Word vector shapes (drawing groups) inside the cells, so no image files or post-processing are needed. Graphics are stored as placeholders until knitting, so print it or knit it as is; flextable functions that restyle the table (e.g. flextable::fontsize()) keep them, but flextable::save_as_docx() and other officer exports do not draw them. When printed or knitted to HTML, the graphics are drawn as SVG.

Details

  • Continuous variables: by default a horizontal violin plot with an inner boxplot (box = IQR, thick line = median, whiskers to the most extreme values within 1.5 x IQR, dots = outliers beyond that) in the variable's label row, above the numeric summaries. All columns share the same x-axis (and violin width) scale so groups are directly comparable. Each violin has the same area (like ggplot2::geom_violin()'s default), so a violin's width shows the shape of that group's distribution, not its sample size; N is given in each column header.

  • Categorical and binary variables: a percentage bar next to each n (%).

Percentages are column percentages (within each group), so bars are comparable across groups. Category percentages exclude missing values, so for variables with missing values counts are shown as n / N (%) with N the non-missing count (see show_denominator); the "N missing" row gives % missing out of all observations in the column. A table note states this whenever it matters.

References

Furmaga J, et al. A new type of table one: showing instead of telling. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. 2026;196.

Examples

# Simulated cohort: group, two continuous, two categorical variables
set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(
  grp = sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 200, TRUE),
  age = rnorm(200, 60, 15),
  los = rlnorm(200, 5, 0.8),
  sex = sample(c("Female", "Male"), 200, TRUE),
  diabetes = rbinom(200, 1, 0.4)
)

# Same data with some missing values
df_miss <- df
df_miss$los[sample(200, 30)] <- NA
df_miss$sex[sample(200, 12)] <- NA

# ---- Defaults ----

# Whole cohort: one column of summaries with inline graphics
table1viz(df)

# Word: in a Quarto document with `format: docx`, table1viz() returns an
# editable Word table automatically. Force it elsewhere with:
if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("xml2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  table1viz(df, name_groupvar = "grp", output = "flextable")
}

# Choose your own ticks for some variables (names become tick labels)

  df,
  name_groupvar = "grp",
  axis_breaks = list(
    age = c(0, 50, 100),
    los = c("0" = 0, "1 yr" = 365, "3 yrs" = 1095, "5 yrs" = 1825)
  )
)
